correctness.rationale: Six pairwise independent normals and widths (2,2,2,1,1,1) define 18n+6 lines for n positive divisible by six. For each of 57 direction subsets, the finite intersection locus is a lattice-point count in nP_S with covolume 1/gcd(pair determinants); vertices of 6P_S are lattice integral, so Ehrhart yields exact quadratic counts. Exact rational 57-polygon area sums (132,72,27,7,1) and complete n=6 pair intersection census determine every linear coefficient; binomial inversion gives the five finite multiplicity polynomials. Three infinity points have 4n+1 and three have 2n+1 branches. Direct exact pair counts at n=6,12 independently recovered incidence counts and both Chern polynomials. Eterovic–Figueroa–Urzua density lemma then gives the claimed accumulation interval, not a finite slope realization.

evidence: Eterović, Figueroa and Urzúa, On the geography of line arrangements (https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.00990): Lemma 4.2, Example 4.5 endpoint 19/8; relevant hypotheses include positive quadratic c1bar growth.

originality.rationale: Root-system/deformed Catalan-type arrangements share normal directions and Ehrhart geometry. Equal-width six-direction construction is not the same weighted window family; incidence multiplicities are width-dependent. The prior density lemma is acknowledged and applies after this paper-specific exact census. It cannot imply the new endpoint without the six-direction area and incidence data; Ehrhart alone does not calculate the coefficients. Best-of-knowledge priority risk remains explicit; unsuccessful search alone is not claimed as proof of novelty.
residual_risks: A deformed Catalan/arrangement characteristic-polynomial census under another parameterization could supply the same six-width incidence table.
Only multiples of six are covered; no optimality of endpoint 197/81 is claimed.
